description: Geospatial Liquefaction Model for California Developed using Ensemble Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) Modeling is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Maggie Roberts, Tufts University (tufts.edu). This project contains a dataset of mapped liquefaction surface manifestation hazard across California for a suite of peak ground velocity (PGV) values from 3 cm/s to 100 cm/s. The maps were developed using the Roberts et al. (2026, in review) ensemble geospatial maximum entropy (MaxEnt) liquefaction model. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 1 top-level file. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-exfz-ma94. Keywords: liquefaction, maximum entropy, hazard mapping, geospatial modeling, ensemble modeling, California. Published 2026-05-27. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
